stories.summary: Nvidia's stock continued to slide on Monday following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia stock falls as investors price in fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation
sources.text: Nvidia 's stock slid 4.12% Monday in the wake of CEO Jensen Huang 's resignation , leading a broader chipmaker selloff after the chip giant lost hundreds of billions in market cap last week. The continued decline since Huang's resignation brought Nvidia's stock to its lowest close since July 1, 2025. Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company's board announced on Thursday, after mounting scrutiny following reports that he had a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8. It was later reported that Huang had romantic relationships with two Nvidia employees. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Friday. An online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has drawn more than 170,000 signatures , as prominent tech executives, including Elon Musk , rallied behind him. A source familiar with the matter told CNBC, however, that Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Huang. Meanwhile, U.S. lawmakers are pushing to launch comprehensive investigations into the scandal. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led the company through its meteoric rise to becoming the world's most valuable company, with its AI chips underpinning the technology's boom. Nvidia appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and said its board would consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent successor. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia, adding that the board should look outside the company for its next chief executive. He also suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls. — CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Jensen Huang says he ‘would be honored’ to return as CEO in first statement since resigning from Nvidia
sources.text: Hours before Nvidia reports its first quarterly results without him, and with reports swirling that a Sam Altman-style resurrection is desired in some areas of Silicon Valley, Jensen Huang told the board he’s available to come back if they want. In his first statement since he resigned last week, the former CEO said he would love to return to the company, but only if its board asked him to. The company has lost $450 billion in market value since he admitted the affair, and a person familiar told CNBC on Monday the board isn’t considering bringing him back while it runs a national security investigation into his conduct. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang wrote in a post on X late Tuesday morning. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” In the post, Huang said he erred in his personal life and “created problems” for everyone involved. He wrote that he owns his mistakes and will cooperate with the board’s independent investigation. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely.” Huang resigned Thursday, ending 33 years as CEO. Days earlier, after he admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials deemed a Chinese spy, the board had backed him, saying on Sunday it had “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team” while announcing an independent investigation. Then on Wednesday, The New York Times reported that five Nvidia employees had alleged Huang was romantically involved with a subordinate, Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, and Reuters reported the board was meeting to consider removing him. Nvidia didn’t give a reason for his departure. After he resigned, Reuters reported he had also had an intimate relationship with another employee. Neither Nvidia nor Huang has confirmed. A campaign to bring Huang back began almost immediately. Before Nvidia announced the departure, Elon Musk said hiring Huang would be an honor and backed the reinstatement drive, writing on X: “A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.” An open letter with more than 170,000 signatures, backed by Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, says Huang deserves due process, “not mob justice.” The petition lists about 8,800 people who identify as current Nvidia employees and 94,000 shareholders, though those affiliations weren’t verified. In Taipei, the Taipei 101 tower displayed messages Monday including “Taiwan Loves Jensen.” Investors also joined in. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker wrote to the board asking it to keep all options open, including Huang’s return. Polymarket bettors gave him a 40% chance of rejoining Nvidia by December 2027. His allies have also formed a “war room” to lobby for his reinstatement. It even went to the White House, when on Monday, President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning to Nvidia, adding, “A lot of people are asking Jensen, they think Jensen should go back.” Trump said Huang had “learned a big lesson,” though he also repeated his support for former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a successor. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pushing the other way. He said that if Nvidia were a bank, “a lot of the executives would be removed.” The decision belongs to Nvidia’s board, which so far has shown no interest. A person familiar told CNBC on Monday that the board isn’t considering bringing Huang back and is focused on a national security investigation into his conduct. Currently, CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, and she and top engineer Ian Buck are seen as possible permanent picks. When Huang left, Nvidia had no president, no chief operating officer and no obvious No. 2. Huang will sit for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 with the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter follows on Dec. 2.

sources.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he’s open to returning in first statement since resignation
sources.text: In his first public statement since resigning as Nvidia CEO last week, Jensen Huang struck a contrite tone, saying that he is committed to cooperating with the board's investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence contact. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said in the written statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber. "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation." Huang said he had seen support from investors and employees and was willing to come back as CEO to help the company navigate "complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics." "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang said in the statement. Sources told CNBC Monday that the board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO. Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO, putting together an online petition with more than 180,000 signatures. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia. Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang, Nvidia's founder, admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had a liason with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence. Jensen Huang also reportedly had romances with employees at Nvidia. Nvidia is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter earnings on Tuesday. Its board of directors said on Friday that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets. Over the past week, I've been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life's work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation. Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours. Correction: Jensen Huang is the former CEO of Nvidia. His title was misstated in a headline on an earlier version of this article.

sources.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
sources.text: Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang . Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes , investing in chips to train AI earlier than most. But just as he’s leaving , the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia , where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great. “Everything sold today was designed two to three years ago,” says the CEO of a large AI company, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says. Already, competitors have started to move in. Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026. Big US cloud players—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—are all developing more specialized chips to power the training and serving of AI models. Each has seen similar gains. These companies are designing their own silicon to reduce costs and to gain some independence from Nvidia. Several startups now offer more specialized chips that promise improvements over Nvidia’s core products. Cerebras, for instance, sells giant ones meant to power giant AI models. AMD recently bought Taalas, a company that burns models’ weights into silicon to make computations ultra efficient. Using these chips requires rewriting a lot of code, however, to make them work with cutting-edge AI models. Patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at MoorInStrat, a company that tracks the chip industry, says the rise of AI agents makes inference, or running models that have already been trained, more important. That’s an area where Nvidia has less of an edge compared to cloud hyperscalers and startups. Nvidia did, however, acquire a startup making specialized chips, called Groq, in December of 2025. And because of the rise in AI assistants and agents, there’s also growing demand for general purpose central processing units (CPUs), Moorhead said, an area where Nvidia barely competes. Nvidia still maintains a huge lead in AI thanks to Huang’s foresight. Huang cofounded the company in 1993 to design graphics chips for PCs. In the mid-2010s, he saw the promise of AI. He funded academic research on the topic, developed software to support AI engineering, and gave hardware to labs and startups. In 2022, ChatGPT took AI mainstream and sales of Nvidia chips skyrocketed. The company’s revenue went from $26.91 billion in January 2022 to $215.94 billion in January 2026. The challenges it faces may not be existential—but they do add up, especially on a global scale. While Nvidia’s fortunes have risen in the US, they have declined in the world’s other big market for AI: China. Washington is trying to restrict access to its most advanced chips, while Beijing is trying to develop its own chip industry. Nvidia is not allowed to sell its most powerful chips in China, but it can sell previous generations. Sales of these chips as well as non AI chips doubled over the past year, but China now accounts for only eight percent of the company’s overall revenue, compared with 20 percent in 2024, according to its fillings. It remains unclear how many chips exported to other countries may either end up in China or end up being used remotely by Chinese firms. Huawei, a Chinese tech giant targeted with US sanctions for several years, has developed new kinds of supercomputers that harness many more chips than usual to train and run AI models. Some Chinese AI companies, such as Z.ai, which makes one of the world’s best open source models, say they’ve trained their models entirely using Huawei’s chips. If Chinese open-weight models gain traction in other countries, it could create a market for Chinese chips elsewhere. Huang’s dealings with China played a major role in his downfall. He had a romantic relationship with Huang Le, also known as Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed who the US government suspects of being an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed and its subsidiaries have reportedly imported between $4.6 and $7.5 billion Nvidia chips into southeast Asia. Reports suggest that the company may have provided access to the chips to Chinese AI firms. Babak Minovi, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, a consultancy that focuses on technology and geopolitics, says Huang was right to point out that cutting off access to China would empower domestic rivals. “Huang was taking a pragmatic line, and he knows competition,” he says. Even in markets that it dominates, Nvidia may turn out to be a victim of its own success. The AI models built using Nvidia’s chip are automating the very elements of coding, data analysis, and scientific research that help design chips. Most chip design firms use specialized AI models to arrange components on processors—something that traditionally required deep engineering expertise and experience. And both OpenAI and Anthropic have recently touted the ability of their newest models to design electronics from scratch. Moorhead says the shift towards AI chip design may not pose a huge threat to Nvidia because it’s riding the same wave. “They have access to AI too,” he notes. But Moorhead says the way AI models can now quickly rewrite code to run on different hardware may prove a problem. For years, Nvidia has attracted developers by providing software that makes it easy to write programs and build models for its silicon. sources.title: NVIDIA establishes export control committee following Jensen Huang resignation
sources.text: The company’s existing global trade compliance team will report to the new committee. Following Jensen Huang's resignation last week , NVIDIA's board of directors has established a new oversight committee to oversee the company's ongoing compliance with US export controls. Suzanne Nora Johnson , a former Goldman Sachs vice chair and recent NVIDIA board appointee, will lead the new internal organization, dubbed the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. The company's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the new committee, as well as interim CEO Colette Kress , on its day-to-day operations. NVIDIA adds the committee will meet at least once quarterly, with meetings with the company's management included. NVIDIA did not immediately respond to a question from Engadget regarding whether the new committee would have the power to halt sales its compliance staff flags, or if it would merely be limited to escalating such issues to Kress and the company's board of directors. In its press release, NVIDIA did say the committee would include two other directors as members, Stephen Neal and John Dabiri . "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," said Harvey Jones, chairman of NVIDIA's board. According to Alex Jacquez , senior vice president of policy, advocacy and research at the economic think tank Groundwork Collaborative , NVIDIA's decision to create this committee at this specific moment raises the question of why the company needs to implement new protocol if it was previously complying with US export laws. "How much is theater for the board and Trump administration to signal that they're taking this seriously, and how much is actual reevaluation of existing practices is still to be determined," he said. The timing of the announcement comes as NVIDIA and its former CEO face increased scrutiny over the company's compliance with US export controls to China. When reporting of Huang's affair with Alice Huang, a former tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset, first surfaced, NVIDIA's board said it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised." In a joint statement issued Monday alongside the Department of Justice , the US Commence Department said it began to investigating Megaspeed in 2024. Alice Huang took a controlling stake in the Singaporean cloud computing company in 2023 before leaving it in August 2025. For part of that time, the firm was one of NVIDIA's business partners in the Asia-Pacific region. The Commerce Department says it requested documents from NVIDIA involving "direct or indirect" sales to Megaspeed in May 2025. In June of that same year, the company placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list. According to The Information , Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang may have facilitated at least $7.5 billion in NVIDIA GPU sales to China. The former CEO has agreed to a closed-doors, transcribed interview with multiple House committees on December 1 . Update 12:15PM ET : Added commentary from Alex Jacquez, senior vice president of policy, advocacy and research at Groundwork Collective.

sources.text: In the first public statement since his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang signaled his willingness to return as CEO if the board decides it is in the company’s best interest. Huang’s statement, posted in full on X , reads as follows: Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours. Jensen Huang resigned after reports of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and another with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is suspected of working with Chinese intelligence services. Nvidia’s chip exports have faced intense scrutiny since the revelations, and Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1. In Huang’s absence, Nvidia has formed a new executive committee to oversee export control compliance. Still, many investors and employees associated with Nvidia have called for Huang to return as CEO, at least until an investigation can provide clearer evidence of guilt. An open letter circulated earlier this week attracted the signatures of more than 10,000 current and former Nvidia employees, as well as prominent tech figures like Elon Musk, Amjad Masad, and Travis Kalanick. “We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the letter reads. “If the Board believes his continued absence is necessary, provide a specific, evidence-based explanation of why it serves NVIDIA’s best interests.” Still, many see such a return as unlikely. On Monday, an unnamed source on Nvidia’s board told The Washington Post there were no plans to reinstate Huang. There’s also significant resistance to the idea in Congress, where Huang still faces significant questions about his role in chip exports to China-linked firms. stories.title: How to Distill Gemini Into an Edge Model
stories.summary: Turn Gemini’s annotations into an edge model for manufacturing inspection. Explore three prompting approaches, review labels, and train RF-DETR model with Roboflow. Deploy the trained model near the camera and keep Gemini available to inspect difficult cases and improve future training data.

sources.title: How to Distill Gemini Into an Edge Model
sources.text: To distill Gemini into an edge model, have Gemini label your images, review and correct those labels, then train a small detector that runs next to the camera and does the routine inspections. In Roboflow, auto-label with Gemini through a class description, the Auto Label agent or an Open Prompt Workflow. Then train RF-DETR Small on the reviewed dataset, run it with Inference on your edge device, and route uncertain cases back to Gemini or a human reviewer. Checking an assembly for missing screws takes more than counting detections. A model might miss one screw and mistake a reflection for another, returning the expected count while overlooking an incomplete product. A useful inspection system needs to locate the visible screws at each mounting position and flag images that need further review. With Roboflow, you can use Gemini to help build the training dataset for that system, then train a compact RF-DETR (opens in a new tab) model to detect screws near the camera. In this approach to model distillation , Gemini generates candidate bounding boxes, you review and correct the annotations, and RF-DETR learns the specific detection task. At deployment, the smaller model handles routine detection, while routing logic sends selected difficult images to Gemini or a person for review. In this guide, you’ll explore three ways to prompt Gemini for screw annotations: class descriptions in Roboflow Auto Label, conversational feedback with the Auto Label agent, and an Open Prompt Workflow that returns boxes for inspection in Python. You’ll then review the labels, train RF-DETR Small, test it on your edge hardware, and configure a fallback for uncertain results. Before generating labels, decide exactly what one object means. In our reference image, each screw annotation covers the full visible fastener region, including its outer exposed end and inner metal feature. One screw receives one box. This definition must stay the same across the dataset. Create an Object Detection project and upload the product images (opens in a new tab) . Include complete products, missing screws, reflections, and realistic changes in lighting. In Roboflow Auto Label (opens in a new tab) , the class description is the prompt Gemini uses to find the object . Follow these steps. Gemini searches using that description, and Auto Label saves each resulting annotation as screw . The expected count of four is an application rule. It should not force the teacher to produce four boxes when a screw is missing. You can also describe the labeling task through Chat with Auto Label agent . The agent builds a labeling Workflow from the model and classes and shows a preview. Use the conversation to refine what it should label. The saved annotations still need a class name, which remains screw in this example. See labeling with the Auto Label agent (opens in a new tab) . With Gemini 4 Carbon selected, open Chat with Auto Label agent and enter the following request. Check the preview and request specific corrections. You can use the following correction when that error appears. You can also click an incorrect label or use Flag missing object. Once the preview matches the annotation rule, choose Use this Workflow, confirm the output-class mapping to screw , and select Label batch. Review the job estimate before starting. Continue with the label review in Section 2. This conversation configures the Auto Label Workflow. Gemini 4 Carbon remains the requested annotation model. Check that the saved Workflow uses it. Either setup option produces the same kind of training data for RF-DETR Small. The training examples contain reviewed screw bounding boxes. For this option, you can choose any Gemini model available in the Roboflow Google Gemini block (opens in a new tab) that supports image input and Open Prompt. You can also try different available models with the same prompt and images to compare their bounding boxes. For the Auto Label process above, Roboflow manages the saved annotations. Use the description field or the Auto Label agent conversation above. Neither option requires you to enter a JSON-format prompt or convert coordinates yourself. If you inspect raw Gemini detection output, Google's official object detection documentation (opens in a new tab) specifies box_2d in [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] order, normalized to 0–1000. Normalization expresses a position relative to the image dimensions. A value of 500 is halfway across the relevant dimension, regardless of image size. Use the following conversion for an image of width W and height H. For example, [100, 200, 300, 250] on a 1000-pixel-wide, 600-pixel-high image gives pixel bounds xmin=200, ymin=60, xmax=250, ymax=180. This is a coordinate example, not a measured screw prediction. Prompting Gemini for boxes in a consistent format gives the visualization code a clear schema to check. Gemini models can still format their answers differently even when they receive the same instructions. This Open Prompt test uses a consistent box_2d schema and a model-independent parser. The prompt requests the screw label and [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] coordinates normalized to 0–1000. The script accepts known JSON formatting differences, but checks the coordinates before drawing them. This follows Gemini’s object-detection coordinate convention (opens in a new tab) . The parser uses the requested coordinate order and scale. Numeric checks alone cannot prove that Gemini followed those instructions, so inspect the drawn boxes. Test with an assembly image and supply the example text in the Workflow’s prompt input. Confirm that both outputs, boxes_json and prompt_echo , appear in the test response. sources.title: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how
sources.text: You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI. Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback. Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road. Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two. To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training. Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes “With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email. Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats. Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history. ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.” Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027 (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.) In all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the company take this step in the right direction. sources.title: Trump says ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security
sources.text: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he does not believe the country’s national security was put at risk as a result of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “It was not put at risk,” Trump said when asked by reporters in light of his own friendship with Huang. “Our country is now stronger than ever before. And you know, China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump went on to contradict previous findings from U.S. officials by doubting that Huang’s paramour, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing on a personal basis what he did … That’s a different story,” Trump added. “But nobody’s proven that she’s a spy. She may not be a spy.” Last year, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw the production of an internal memo, circulated among top policymakers, which warned that Alice Huang was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. Trump was reportedly briefed about these intelligence findings at least twice, including once in May aboard Air Force One, shortly before the former Nvidia CEO joined him on a trip to China. But Trump has maintained that he was not aware of these claims. The U.S. regulates the exports of Nvidia’s top chips to China as a way of maintaining a competitive advantage. But prior to news of Huang’s affair publicly emerging, both the U.S. and Singaporean governments had been investigating Megaspeed for illegally smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Huang has since stepped down from the role he has had for 33 years at Nvidia after more reporting revealed that he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees, at least one of whom was a direct report. Given Huang’s importance to Nvidia, some prominent figures in the industry — including Elon Musk, Y Combinator president and CEO Garry Tan, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney — have signed a public letter calling for Nvidia to reinstate Huang. “A lot of people are asking Jensen — they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” Trump said. Referring to the former Apple chief executive, Trump added: “I recommended Tim Cook.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . sources.title: Nvidia’s first big move after Jensen Huang’s exit targets national security
sources.text: Nvidia has formed a committee to oversee national security policies and export control compliance following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who had links to one of the company’s customers. Nvidia said Tuesday that the new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks. The move comes amid increased scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Huang’s alleged ties to the suspected spy and his advocacy for easing restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China. The Commerce Department said Monday it was planning to introduce new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside of the U.S. in an effort to prevent companies in China and elsewhere from circumventing existing rules by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. The interim rule was made in direct response to the unfolding chip smuggling scandal at Nvidia. The announcement comes just a few hours before Nvidia’s highly anticipated third-quarter earnings call. Analysts, the media, and shareholders expect the company to address the controversy and outline how it might affect operations. This is the first major action by the company under the leadership of Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who took over as interim CEO after Huang stepped down last week. The committee, which will meet at least quarterly, will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and include fellow directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. Nvidia already has a national security team and global trade compliance team. Those teams will now report to this board committee and Kress on day-to-day operations. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress later this month. sources.title: Nvidia reveals new national security and export committee after CEO's exit
sources.text: Where was this when Nvidia's booming profits kicked off during the rise of generative AI? Update, November 17: Since this story was published, former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang released his first statement on X since resigning from the company. He says that "if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." You can read the full statement below. Original story follows... Nvidia has formed a new 'National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee' in the wake of the resignation of Jensen Huang . A press release from the board explains that the committee will be "responsible for board-level oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management." Nvidia already has a National Security Team and a Global Trade Compliance Team, both of which will now report to this committee (as well as reporting to interim CEO Colette Kress), keeping them up to speed on day-to-day operations, we're told. The committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, will meet at least every quarter, and it'll be advised by "independent third-party experts" in law, national security, and trade compliance. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said: "Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security." He added that: "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation." Did someone say damage control? Clearly, Nvidia is a firm that's reeling from the exit of its CEO, and as you've doubtless seen, this has been a controversial matter for a number of reasons. Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. While Huang has admitted to having an affair, the allegations around it being with a Chinese spy remain just that – allegations – and there's been no proof of this. So, while this new committee isn't a reaction to this side of the controversy – not as such, as it remains unproven – it is obviously enough a move to shore up any doubt there might be as to Nvidia's stance on national security and global trade therein. Some of the reaction on Reddit has been predictable, and indeed there's a level of incredulity that Nvidia didn't already have this in place. However, it's worth noting the details here – as the press release states, Nvidia does indeed have teams dedicated to national security and global trade compliance. Of course, every big tech company has considerable assets in place to guard their intellectual property, and we've also seen Nvidia's export controls in action with the RTX 5090 and China as the most high-profile example (and indeed more broadly in the data center sphere) . What's new with the committee here is that it has oversight across those existing entities, theoretically tightening everything up and bringing in independent experts. Although of course, you could further argue that this should have been in place already on top of the compliance teams. And there are certainly more than a few comments along the same lines as this Redditor's observation : "Horses are already down the road, I better shut the gate..." Meanwhile, support for the return of Jensen Huang continues to grow, but Nvidia's board is reportedly unmoved – he won't be coming back as CEO, we're told .
